title: Affine morphism gives a quasi-coherent derived equivalence
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Regard $f_*\mathcal O_X$ as an $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra. Then $Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] induces an equivalence $\Phi:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], where the target is the full subcategory of the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $f_*\mathcal O_X$-modules on $Y$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] consisting of the complexes whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent $f_*\mathcal O_X$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-correspondence], and the composition of $\Phi$ with the restriction functor $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ is $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$. The affine module correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-correspondence] identifies quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-modules, via $f_*$. Regard this equivalence as the underived direct image for the ringed-space morphism $g$.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, reduction to the affine module correspondence

proof.text: The morphism $g$ is flat: on affine stalks it is the localization map $\mathcal A_q\to\mathcal O_{X,p}$. Thus $g^*=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal A}g^{-1}(-)$ is exact on the relevant quasi-coherent objects. By the displayed definition of $Lg^*$, a K-flat resolution $P\to M$ computes it, and exactness gives $H^i(Lg^*M)=g^*H^i(M)$ by applying $g^*$ to kernels and images. The ringed-space adjunction [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general] gives $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$. First restrict this adjunction's direct image to the underlying schemes: Step 4 identifies the restriction of $Rg_*$ with $Rf_*$. Therefore [lem-sc-affine-derived-cohomology] gives $H^i(Rg_*K)=f_*H^i(K)$, since restriction of scalars is exact and does not change cohomology sheaves. The affine correspondence makes these sheaves quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-modules, so $Rg_*$ lands in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, derived equivalence and cohomology comparison

proof.text: For $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal A)$, the same exact-localization calculation gives $H^i(Lg^*M)=g^*H^i(M)$ and preserves quasi-coherence. The correspondence's $h(G)=f^*G\otimes_{f^*\mathcal A}\mathcal O_X$ agrees naturally with $g^*G$: $h(G)=(\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}G)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X\otimes f^{-1}\mathcal A}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}f^{-1}G=g^*G$. Since $g^*$ and $g_*$ are exact on the relevant objects, the cohomology maps of the derived unit and counit are the underived maps $H^i(M)\to g_*g^*H^i(M)$ and $g^*g_*H^i(K)\to H^i(K)$. They are respectively the affine correspondence's $\beta_{H^i(M)}$ and $\alpha_{H^i(K)}$, hence isomorphisms. Thus $Lg^*$ and $Rg_*$ are mutually quasi-inverse.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, unit and counit of the affine derived equivalence

proof.text: Restriction of scalars along $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal A$ is exact because it does not change the underlying sheaf or its kernels and cokernels. By [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $K$; both $Rg_*K$ and $Rf_*K$ are represented by the same underlying complex $f_*I$, with only the module structure changed. The scheme-level derived direct image is the functor in [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Hence restriction of $\Phi=Rg_*$ is canonically $Rf_*$, and this comparison is used in Step 2 before applying the affine cohomology formula.

The proof now uses g:(X,O_X)->(Y,f_*O_X), proves the derived equivalence via the Lg^* -| Rg_* adjunction and affine module correspondence, and identifies restriction of Rg_* with Rf_* without treating termwise pushforward on arbitrary complexes as exact.
